title: Prove the sharp cost of replacing all 537 BIT sink ingresses
body:
The incumbent 537 sink directions attain sharp minimum cost at both trials. A weighted matching proof covers arbitrary additional or replacement paid direct arrivals, same-start helper retargets, and a rebuilt terminal decoder on the fixed historical stock.

## Scope and source

Checks all 635 nonsink banks and 20 source groups, with fixed exterior packet values and routes and protected main and 411 terminals. No upstream stock changes are charged or assumed. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit-sink-matching/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. `python3 -IB verify.py` passed from a fresh extraction. An independent raw-tape implementation reproduced all directed comparisons and both receipts byte for byte, and detected a synthetic cheaper route. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

A positive repair must change nonsink stock, the allowed owner interface, or another part of the full invoice.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
